key_insight: NeutronGym turns neutron instrument design into an executable, physics-graded benchmark that can measure whether LLM agents truly reason about physics rather than memorize answers.
engineering_relevance: The environment provides a trustworthy way to evaluate and train agents for scientific instrument design, with potential use in automated experimental planning and model-based engineering workflows.
method: Agents construct neutron instruments using validating tools.
McStas ray-traces each design and a level-resolved ladder scores syntax, runtime, structure, and scientific performance without an LLM judge.
Procedural families and held-out parameter regimes create scalable, controlled evaluation; McStasBench adds 16 published-instrument tasks with memorization probes.
evidence_signal: Seven models solved at most 7 of 16 benchmark tasks, while RL on the environment's reward improved Qwen3-8B from 11% to 77% on held-out instances and transferred to additional gated families.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on the benchmark's reward design and simulation budget, and the paper notes that careful task design was needed to avoid unsolved baselines and misleading evaluations.
paper_title: NeutronGym: Physics-Graded Neutron Instrument Design for LLM Agents
